verification: Actual runs used AWS 6.68.0 with official Terraform 1.15.9 and 1.16.6. ZIP, layer, URL and OCI bytes passed. Seven native imports, updates, prior-version isolation and controller reopen passed. All ordinary no-change plans returned 0. Three strict refresh-only plans returned 2 on both cores. The parent isolated an external Core data-state whitespace defect without a provider or service. These assertions still fail. The final run destroyed 17 managed resources. Signed Lambda, layer, ECR, IAM and log-group absence checks passed. No managed Terraform resources remained.
classification_policy: Source registrations describe subsets, not provider parity. Actual evidence applies only to the exercised fixture settings and stages. Unrun registrations, settings and native consumers remain unverified. Unsupported means an absent operation or rejected execution path. Uncalibrated means implemented source with no actual evidence from this fixture.

corrections: Lambda accepts SnapStart ApplyOn=None (disabled) and empty EFS clear requests rather than conflating them with unsupported snapshot/EFS execution. PublishedVersions and nonempty EFS remain explicit errors.

ECR PutImageScanningConfiguration and PutRegistryScanningConfiguration reject enabling scan_on_push without real scanner/database, matching CreateRepository instead of recording metadata-only scan success.
The layer version output uses tonumber for the signed SDK absence check.
Short-lived ECR credentials use separate state. The infrastructure plan does not own token timestamps.
data_plane_boundary: Fixture publishes real OCI image config and gzipped tar blobs through signed InitiateLayerUpload/UploadLayerPart/CompleteLayerUpload/PutImage. Independent consumer retrieves registry manifests/blobs under Basic auth and SDK layer download URLs, validates descriptor digests/sizes/rootfs diff IDs, and compares extracted binary payload. This does not claim Docker registry pull/run or ECR-to-Lambda image execution. Lambda fixture executes actual ZIP bytes through official RIC independently of the OCI artifact.
prerequisites: AWS provider exactly 6.68.0 and the checked-in checksum lock
Docker-backed Lambda with installed official runtime and storage images plus matching telemetry helpers
Use a fresh fixture-owned controller. The fixture reopens its database and destroys its IAM prerequisites.
procedure: Initialize the exact AWS provider version with the checked-in checksum lock.
Create the owned IAM role, network-independent Lambda resources and ECR repository.
Push the first real OCI manifest and blob bytes into the owned registry.
Consume actual Lambda, URL, layer and authenticated OCI bytes through independent clients.
Save strict refresh-only and ordinary no-change plans. Require exit 0 and retain every failed assertion.
Import all seven owned native identities without replacing their live resources.
Apply the code, environment, alias and layer update. Push the second OCI image.
Require second revision bytes through the updated alias and URL. Require first bytes through the prior published version.
Require the prior OCI digest to retain its manifest. Delete that digest through signed BatchDeleteImage.
Stop and reopen the same owned controller database. Repeat both retained Lambda-version consumers and OCI consumers.
Save both strict no-change plans again. Retain failed assertions until normal cleanup completes.
Use ordinary Terraform destroy for all declared resources, including the nonempty owned ECR repository.
Check signed Lambda, layer, ECR, IAM and log-group absence. Check empty managed Terraform state.
